title: Naturality and common-resolution descent for resolved total comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and use ordinary derived categories, localization $Q$, and the K-injective right derived functor $RF$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $\Delta$ have the finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]$ and order-preserving maps as its objects and arrows. For a strict functor $C:\Delta\to\operatorname{Ch}^{\ge0}(\mathcal A)$, put $T(C)^r=\bigoplus_{n+q=r}C_n^q$ and $d_T=\delta+(-1)^n d_C$, where $\delta=\sum_i(-1)^i C(d^i)$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Let $u:K\to J$ and $v:L\to M$ be strict columnwise quasi-isomorphisms with $J_n,M_n$ nonnegative termwise injective complexes, and put $\chi_u=Q\beta_J\rho_{T(J)}RF(QT(u))$ and $\chi_v=Q\beta_M\rho_{T(M)}RF(QT(v))$, where $\beta$ is the summand-preserving finite-total chain isomorphism and $\rho$ the inverse right-derived unit. For every strict square $gu=vf$, with $f:K\to L$ and $g:J\to M$, one has
$$QT(Fg)\chi_u=\chi_v RF(QT(f)).$$
The column comparisons satisfy $QF(g_n)c_{u_n}=c_{v_n}RF(Qf_n)$, with $c_{u_n}=\rho_{J_n}RF(Qu_n)$. Thus these total maps represent the strict derived-image maps on columns, and identities and composites agree. For two replacements $u:K\to J$ and $w:K\to N$, and any functorial nonnegative injective resolution $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to I$ of complexes, the strict zigzag
$$J\xrightarrow{\eta_J}I(J)\xleftarrow{I(u)}I(K)\xrightarrow{I(w)}I(N)\xleftarrow{\eta_N}N$$
has columnwise quasi-isomorphisms, and applying $T(F(-))$ gives quasi-isomorphisms on every leg. Its induced isomorphism $e_{u,w}:QT(FJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}QT(FN)$ is $\chi_w\chi_u^{-1}$. It is independent of $I$ and of every augmentation-preserving zigzag through nonnegative termwise injective columns whose intermediate augmented objects are also columnwise quasi-isomorphic replacements of $K$; $e_{u,u}=1$ and $e_{w,z}e_{u,w}=e_{u,z}$. These identifications commute with the strict-square equation above. The terms K-injective, quasi-isomorphism and injective resolution have the meanings of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-sp-injective-resolutions].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-injective-finite-total-derived-comparison] to each replacement $u:K\to J$ and $v:L\to M$. It gives the quasi-isomorphisms $T(u),T(v)$, the K-injective nonnegative totals $T(J),T(M)$, the column comparisons $c_{u_n},c_{v_n}$, and the isomorphisms $\chi_u,\chi_v$ with exactly the normalization in the statement. In particular all inverses used below exist. Its finite-biproduct comparison also gives $T(Fg)\beta_J=\beta_MF(T(g))$ for every strict map $g:J\to M$; no quasi-isomorphism assumption on $g$ is needed.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha_E:QF(E)\to RF(QE)$ for the unit of the total right derived functor [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], a natural transformation $Q\circ F\Rightarrow RF\circ Q$ on all complexes. For nonnegative termwise injective $E,E'$ the comparison in step 1 identifies $\rho_E=\alpha_E^{-1}$. Naturality of the unit is, by definition of natural transformation, $RF(Qh)\alpha_E=\alpha_{E'}QF(h)$ for every chain map $h:E\to E'$. Multiply by $\alpha_{E'}^{-1}$ on the left and $\alpha_E^{-1}$ on the right to obtain
$$QF(h)\rho_E=\rho_{E'}RF(Qh).$$
We will use this identity for $h=T(g)$ and $h=g_n$. This is just inversion of the naturality square, not a claim that $F$ preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic) and 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor): inverse derived unit and finite-total comparison; explicit naturality calculation.

proof.text:
Totalization respects composition on each summand, so $gu=vf$ gives $T(g)T(u)=T(v)T(f)$. Using steps 1 and 2, calculate
$$\begin{aligned}QT(Fg)\chi_u&=Q\beta_M\,QF(T(g))\rho_{T(J)}RF(QT(u))\\&=Q\beta_M\rho_{T(M)}RF(Q(T(g)T(u)))\\&=\chi_vRF(QT(f)).\end{aligned}$$
In each column, the same multiplication without $\beta$ gives $QF(g_n)c_{u_n}=\rho_{M_n}RF(Q(g_nu_n))=c_{v_n}RF(Qf_n)$. Thus the column maps represent the strict derived-image maps. For two composable squares their equations multiply to give the equation for the composite, and the identity square gives the identity: this follows from the functor laws for $RF$ and $T(F(-))$.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic) and 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor): inverse derived unit and finite-total comparison; explicit naturality calculation.

proof.text: Now fix the functor $I$ and natural quasi-isomorphism $\eta$ quantified in the statement. Postcomposition by a functor preserves all cosimplicial identities; naturality of $\eta$ gives strict maps of diagrams. Give the five objects $J,I(J),I(K),I(N),N$ their augmentations from $K$, respectively $u,\eta_Ju,\eta_K,\eta_Nw,w$. The four zigzag legs preserve these augmentations because $I(u)\eta_K=\eta_Ju$ and $I(w)\eta_K=\eta_Nw$. Each augmentation is columnwise a quasi-isomorphism. In each column, the same two equations show that $I(u)$ and $I(w)$ are quasi-isomorphisms: applying every $H^r$, their composites with the invertible $H^r(\eta_K)$ are invertible. The other two legs are components of $\eta$ and are quasi-isomorphisms by assumption. Every object in this zigzag has nonnegative termwise injective columns, including $I(K)$ by the stipulated property of $I$.

source.place: Tag 0141, lemma-functorial-injective-resolutions and remark-match: natural augmentation squares; only the functorial resolution given in the statement is used.

proof.text:
Let $h:A\to B$ be any strict columnwise quasi-isomorphism between diagrams with nonnegative termwise injective columns. Applying [lem-sfb-injective-finite-total-derived-comparison] with replacement $h$ shows that $T(h)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $T(B)$ is a bounded-below complex of injectives; applying it with replacement $1_A$ shows the same for $T(A)$. So both totals have invertible derived units $\rho_{T(A)},\rho_{T(B)}$. Step 2 therefore gives
$$QF(T(h))=\rho_{T(B)}RF(QT(h))\rho_{T(A)}^{-1},$$
an isomorphism. The finite-total naturality square gives
$$QT(Fh)=Q\beta_B\,QF(T(h))\,(Q\beta_A)^{-1},$$
also an isomorphism. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], every cohomology functor factors through $Q$; applying it shows that every $H^r(T(Fh))$ is invertible, exactly the definition of quasi-isomorphism. This proves the required assertion for all four legs, and for any leg between augmented replacements in the stated class.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic) and 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor): inverse derived unit and finite-total comparison; explicit naturality calculation.

proof.text: For a forward augmentation-preserving leg $h:A\to B$ between replacements $a:K\to A$ and $b:K\to B$, use step 3 with $f=1_K$. Since $ha=b$, it gives $QT(Fh)\chi_a=\chi_b$, hence $QT(Fh)=\chi_b\chi_a^{-1}$. A backward leg contributes the inverse, $\chi_a\chi_b^{-1}$. Multiplying these expressions along the displayed zigzag cancels every intermediate comparison, leaving $e_{u,w}=\chi_w\chi_u^{-1}$. The same cancellation works for every finite augmentation-preserving zigzag whose intermediate augmentations are columnwise quasi-isomorphic injective replacements. Its value depends only on $u,w$, so is independent both of the zigzag and of $I$. Direct multiplication gives $e_{u,u}=1$ and $e_{w,z}e_{u,w}=\chi_z\chi_u^{-1}=e_{u,z}$.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic) and 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor): inverse derived unit and finite-total comparison; explicit naturality calculation.

proof.text:
Finally fix a strict $f:K\to L$, two source replacements $u,u'$ and two target replacements $v,v'$, with strict lifts $g,g'$ of $f$. Step 3 writes their mapped total morphisms as $QT(Fg)=\chi_vRF(QT(f))\chi_u^{-1}$ and $QT(Fg')=\chi_{v'}RF(QT(f))\chi_{u'}^{-1}$. Using step 6, both
$$e_{v,v'}QT(Fg)\quad\text{and}\quad QT(Fg')e_{u,u'}$$
are $\chi_{v'}RF(QT(f))\chi_u^{-1}$. This is the claimed compatibility of the choice identifications with strict-square naturality.
